value: When cleared straight-in, when arriving on a NoPT route or sector, when radar vectored to final, or on a timed approach.
reason: The back gave only the straight-in clearance, but the same AIM paragraph says no procedure turn is required on a NoPT route and bars one after radar vectors or on a timed approach; the deck's own no-pt-cases and app-no-pt cards say so.

value: A depicted course reversal is part of the approach, so it is flown unless something removes it: a straight-in clearance, a NoPT route, or a radar vector or timed approach, when it needs ATC clearance.
reason: Explains why the other cases remove the procedure turn, in line with AIM 5-4-9.

value: How high a minimum sits above the touchdown zone elevation, as a height instead of an altitude above sea level.
reason: 'Printed beside the altitude on an approach chart' is not in the cited Part 97 entry, which only expands the abbreviation; the new back keeps to the term and the IPH use of HAT above TDZE.

value: Older systems measure it with transmissometers on towers along the runway; newer ones use forward scatter sensors. Values are given in feet.
reason: AIM 7-1-13 says New Generation RVR, replacing the transmissometer systems, uses forward scatter technology.

value: At standard rate, as soon as instructed; on final of a surveillance or precision approach, at half standard rate once told.
reason: AIM 5-4-11 says the pilot is advised to use half standard rate after the turn onto final on a surveillance or precision approach; the back made it automatic.

value: C: LP is published only where a vertically guided procedure cannot be, and it has no glidepath. B: LP is a lateral guidance line.
reason: 'Never published alongside a vertically guided line' goes beyond the AIM, which says LP is published only if a vertically guided procedure cannot be.

value: A: that divides the FAF altitude alone by the time, ignoring the touchdown zone elevation. C: 800 feet per minute for 2 minutes loses only 1,600 of the 2,000 feet.
reason: 'Divides too much height by too much time' does not show where 800 comes from or why it is wrong.

value: Like a ledge you must stay on until you can see the path down, but on an approach it holds until the runway references are in sight.
reason: 'A ceiling height you may not duck below' pictures an upper limit, while an MDA is a floor.

value: The fix where the initial approach segment begins.
reason: Section 1.1 says an approach may also begin at the start of a defined arrival route, so 'and so the published approach' overstates.

value: Like the start line of a marked trail, but for an approach: the fix where the initial segment begins.
reason: Matches the corrected back; an approach can also begin from a defined arrival route.

value: The handbook flies the pattern at similar altitudes, airspeeds and key positions to a two-engine approach.
reason: The source says 'similar', not the same.
